# Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API

# Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Fee-free status is a per-market setting that Lighter has changed before. All RWA perp markets traded with 0 fees across every fee and staking tier in March 2026, and in April 2026 RWA market fees turned back on, applied based on tier. In April 2026 Lighter added is_taker_fee_enabled and is_maker_fee_enabled fields to the orderBookDetails endpoint so clients can verify markets where fees are disabled, and said only $LIT had maker fees set to zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-18) — https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/104 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/121, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/122
- [statement] A Lighter API key is a keypair separate from the Ethereum key. Each key is bound to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and has its own nonce stream. Usable key indexes are 4 to 254. Indexes 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's apps (on Robinhood Chain, 157 is also reserved), and 255 is only for querying all keys. Registering a key uses ChangePubKey, which always needs an L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/wasm-signer.md

## How it works

- [statement] In a November 2026 announcement Lighter said new per-IP WebSocket limits take effect on Lighter Core after the scheduled downtime on Sunday, November 22. Standard / public, Plus and base Premium get 50 connections, 1,000 subscriptions, 200 unique accounts and 200 client messages per 60 seconds. Premium 1 and above get 255 connections, 5,000 subscriptions, 5,000 unique accounts and 1,000 client messages per 60 seconds; Builder gets 255, 10,000, 10,000 and 10,000. Only connections authenticated with the Authorization handshake header receive tier limits, while Plus and base Premium retain Standard limits even when authenticated. The rate-limits docs page still listed the older limits of 255 connections and 5000 subscriptions per IP. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/203 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits, https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/releases/tag/v1.1.9
- [statement] On the morning of November 16 (UTC) an attacker recovered API private keys from public signatures because the affected accounts used unsafe signing code other than the official Lighter SDKs that reused signing nonces, then moved funds through a public pool: create a public pool from the affected account, mint pool shares in a separate attacker-controlled account, transfer the affected account's funds into the pool (increasing NAV without minting pool shares), redeem the shares and withdraw. Lighter says its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. Bitquery traced one withdrawal of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC to a single wallet that swapped it to ETH in four minutes and sent 1,920 ETH through twelve new wallets to Hyperliquid, where each one bought XMR1. (high confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/GoPlusSecurity/status/2122520900046319815, https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack, https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/11/16/lighter-suspends-all-withdrawals-after-usd10-4-million-crypto-exploit, https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/
- [statement] lighter-go v1.0.13 retracts v1.0.1 because GenerateAPIKey with a non-empty seed produced weak, predictable API keys, and tells users to upgrade and rotate any API key generated with a seed. The same release bumps golang.org/x/crypto for a critical vulnerability and requires Go 1.26. (low confidence) — https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-go/releases/tag/v1.0.13
- [statement] Third-party connectors have had real-money defects on Lighter. Hummingbot issue 8504 (state: open) reports Lighter perp market orders that Lighter executed successfully but that Hummingbot recorded as FILLED with executed_amount_base = 0 and no trade fills. The issue notes that trade-history polling queries the market-wide /api/v1/recentTrades endpoint, whose sample BTC-USDC response covered only ~9.5 seconds of market trades, so it can miss the account's fills; whether that happened for these two orders was not established. Hummingbot issue 8309 (now closed) reported repeated 429 Too Many Requests errors on Lighter when perpetual APIs were enabled. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8504 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8309
- [statement] Bubblemaps and Bitquery both report a withdrawal of about $10.39M from Lighter on 16 November 2026. Bubblemaps says the attacker deposited $20k into Lighter and withdrew $10.39M about 36 minutes later. Bitquery traced one transfer of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC, swapped $10.36 million of it to ETH on CoW Swap, and sent ETH to Hyperliquid, where each wallet bought XMR1. Posts on X put the loss at $15.5 million across two market maker accounts; Bitquery says a second amount, reported at $5.09 million, had not left Lighter when it last read the chain. (high confidence) — https://x.com/bubblemaps/status/2122298877566931424 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack
- [statement] An API response with code 200 means the transaction was accepted, not executed. When the outcome is unknown (timeout, dropped connection, no WebSocket confirmation), do not re-sign blindly. Check the transaction status by hash or the account_tx channel, and compare nextNonce with the nonce used. Re-signing with a new nonce while the original may still execute can place the order twice. Reusing the same clientOrderIndex rejects a duplicate only while the first order is still open. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Lighter's troubleshooting page maps symptoms to causes. invalid nonce (21104): two processes use one API key concurrently, or an earlier transaction failed in the sequencer without consuming its nonce; batch nonces must be consecutive (21105). invalid PublicKey, please run changePubKey (21108): the key is not registered at that index, or another app replaced it at the same index. Signature rejected: the chainId must be 304 for mainnet and 300 for testnet. HTTP 429 or 405: rate limited, so back off, authenticate requests, reduce polling (use WebSocket) or change tier. account not found (21100) after a deposit: deposits take a few minutes to credit (CCTP: ~15–20 min). WebSocket disconnects come from no frame within 2 minutes, too many subscriptions, reading too slowly, or a server deployment. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can buy volume quota with USDC on Lighter mainnet through POST /api/v1/buyVolumeQuota at 0.0005 USDC per quota (1,000,000 quota = 500 USDC). A single request can buy at most 15,000,000 quota, and the balance after the purchase must not exceed 30,000,000; trading alone refills the balance only up to 15,000,000. The payment is an L2Transfer that you sign and pass as tx_info. lighter-python users should use client.sign_transfer() to obtain the signed tx_info and not client.transfer(), because it submits the transfer through sendTx, moving the payment asset without purchasing quota. The endpoint is not available on testnet. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/account/accountlimits.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] On Lighter, Standard accounts (the default) pay 0 maker and 0 taker fees on regular perpetual and spot orders. They pay 1 bp (0.01%) on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts are subject to maker and taker fees. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] Standard accounts pay for zero fees in latency: taker orders, cancels and modifies wait 300ms, while maker orders have 0ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have 140 ms taker latency, and their cancels and post-only placements carry no added latency. Premium fees start at 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker, falling by up to 30% (0.0028% / 0.0196%) with 500,000 staked LIT. LIT stake is aggregated per L1 address across sub-accounts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] On a Standard account maker latency is 0ms, while cancel/modify latency is 300ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have no additional latency on cancels and post-only placement. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] Lighter had a serious outage during the October 11, 2025 market-wide liquidation event. Phemex reports three transaction batches were lost and the liquidity pool (LLP) fell 5.35%. Beosin identified dependence on a single sequencer and ZK-SNARK proof generation bottlenecks as key factors, and the CEO admitted a delayed database upgrade hindered the platform. Separately, On Chain Times says that on October 10th LLP took a 5% loss and LLP holders were compensated in points. (medium confidence) — https://phemex.com/news/article/lighter-exchange-outage-amid-19b-crypto-liquidation-28446 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.onchaintimes.com/a-look-into-lighters-llp-recent-performance/
- [statement] Critics argue the zero fee is not free. An HTX-hosted analysis puts the standard account's actual cost at 6-12 basis points per trade, 5-10 times higher than the premium account's 0.2-2 basis points per trade, using typical volatility levels (50–80% annualized) and an informed-trader advantage of 2–5 times. TrueHold gives a comparison: a $10,000 position opened and closed with market orders costs $0 on a Lighter standard account and $5.60 on Premium before discounts, but 300 ms of slippage can cost more than a 0.028% taker fee for traders who take liquidity often in fast markets. (low confidence) — https://www.htx.com/news/the-illusion-of-zero-fees-how-lighter-extracts-costs-through-SkcqJ0ec/ · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] Premium/Advanced is the opt-in tier suitable for HFT, the lowest latency on Lighter. On Lighter mainnet it charges 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker before discounts, gives a 140ms taker delay for all tiers, and adds no latency to cancels or post-only placements. Staking LIT cuts fees by 2.5% at 1,000 LIT up to 30% at 500,000 LIT (0.0028% maker, 0.0196% taker). Stake is summed per L1 address across sub-accounts, and fee credits count as staked LIT. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] Standard accounts have 300ms taker latency, 300ms cancel latency and 0ms post-only latency. Premium removes the delay on cancels and post-only placement and sets the taker delay at 140ms. A batch waits for the longest speed bump of any transaction in it, so mixing a taker order into a batch of post-only orders delays all of them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Plus accounts are the opt-in tier for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits. They pay 0.005% maker and taker, keep 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and 0ms maker latency, and get 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute, 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute and 16 sub-accounts. Standard accounts can create up to 4 sub-accounts, which cannot be deleted. The tier is switched with the `changeAccountTier` endpoint; downgrades require a 24-hour cooldown after the last tier change. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] Lighter mainnet and Lighter on Robinhood Chain have separate base URLs and rate-limit tables. Lighter mainnet uses https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai; Lighter on Robinhood Chain uses https://api.rh.lighter.xyz (chain ID 466324), with Builder 150,000, Plus 120,000 and Premium 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions, https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/blob/main/lighter/signer_client.py
- [statement] On Lighter mainnet, Standard accounts (the default) pay 0 maker and 0 taker on regular perpetual and spot orders. Since an August 2026 change they pay 0.01% (1 bp) on TWAP, Chase Limit and RFQ orders. Plus and Premium accounts continue to pay their normal tier fees. Limit and market orders remain free for Standard accounts, and binary options have a separate fee model. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/163, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] On Lighter mainnet the Plus tier is the opt-in tier for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits. It charges 0.005% maker and taker, keeps the 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and 0ms maker latency, and allows 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute, 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute and 16 sub-accounts. Standard allows 4 sub-accounts and Premium 64, and sub-accounts cannot be deleted. Plus is enabled with the `changeAccountTier` endpoint or in the app. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] REST limits depend on tier. Standard accounts get 60 requests per rolling minute, unweighted, with no separate sendTx bucket. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and read-only endpoints fall into a separate bucket from sendTx and sendTxBatch. Builder accounts, free of charge on application through Discord, get 240,000 weighted requests per rolling minute. Limits apply to both IP address and L1 address, and authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405, and a firewall block lasts 60 seconds. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/119, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/100
- [statement] On a Standard account every call competes for the same 60 requests per minute, including nonce and reconciliation reads, and weight-3,000 endpoints permit only eight calls/minute. Opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) also counts against the REST limit, and once it is exhausted new WebSocket connections receive HTTP 429. NautilusTrader suggests 15 transaction requests and 5 REST calls/minute for bounded Standard testing, and a Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 18, 2026 reports repeated 429 Too Many Requests errors on the Lighter perpetual private websocket connection and candle polling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8309
- [statement] API keys belong to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and each has its own key pair and nonce. Indexes 0–254 exist, 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's web/mobile apps, and 255 is a special index only for querying apikeys. Registering a key requires the L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). A key can trade, cancel, modify, change leverage and margin, create sub-accounts, make secure withdrawals (which can only go back to the L1 address that created the account) and make same-owner transfers. It cannot alone transfer to another L1 owner, fast-withdraw or approve an integrator with fees. Auth tokens last at most 8 hours, and Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md
- [statement] Premium/Advanced accounts can mark up to 251 API keys per account index as maker-only. These keys are restricted to 0ms speed bump transactions only (post-only (ALO) orders, modifies of ALO orders, cancel and cancel all) and get an optimized execution path with reduced scheduling latency. Order types with a speed bump sent via a maker-only key are rejected with error 62007, a 1-hour cooldown applies between api key type changes (error 62008), and Standard accounts are rejected (error 62009). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/114

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Standard accounts face a 60 requests per rolling minute REST limit, unweighted. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and Builder accounts (free, applied for via Discord) get 240,000. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405. A firewall block lasts 60 seconds; an API-server cooldown follows `weightOfEndpoint/(totalWeight/60)`. Opening a WebSocket (weight 90) counts against the REST limit. Authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply instead of IP-based limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits
- [statement] Lighter mainnet and Lighter on Robinhood Chain have separate base URLs and rate-limit tables. Lighter mainnet uses https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai and signing chain ID 304, Lighter on Robinhood Chain uses https://api.rh.lighter.xyz and chain ID 466324, and testnets use 300. In the Robinhood Chain tables, Standard has 200 ms maker/cancel latency and 8 sub-accounts, Plus pays 0.015% with 8000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 120000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium fees and limits follow last 14D volume (0.0120% maker, 0.0350% taker below $1M) instead of staked LIT. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md
- [statement] In October 2025 Lighter said a runaway bot jammed through the HYPE book with size, that there were no liquidations or other adverse effects, and that the wick was scrubbed from the front end. CoinDesk reported that HYPE briefly surged to $98 on Lighter at a steep premium compared to global prices, that all on-chain transaction data remains transparent and accessible on blockchain explorers, and that crypto analyst Duo Nine criticized the removal of the data as masking deeper liquidity issues. (medium confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/1982936377668022508 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/10/28/how-a-bot-glitch-sent-hyperliquid-s-hype-token-soaring-to-usd98
- [statement] The 'zero fee is a latency tax' critique is a model, not a measurement. A MarsBit article (last updated on 2025-12-11) puts the standard account's actual cost at 6-12 basis points per trade versus 0.2-2 basis points on the premium account (5-10 times higher), using typical volatility levels (50–80% annualized) and an informed-trader advantage of 2–5 times. Leviathan News repeated the 5–10× claim on its X account. TrueHold frames the trade-off as a choice: a $10,000 position opened and closed with market orders costs $0 on a Lighter standard account and $5.60 on Premium before discounts, and 300 ms of slippage can cost more than a 0.028% taker fee for traders who take liquidity often in fast markets. (medium confidence) — https://www.htx.com/news/the-illusion-of-zero-fees-how-lighter-extracts-costs-through-SkcqJ0ec/ · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/leviathan_news/status/1999011488283914615, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Lighter auth tokens are signed with an API key and each can have a maximum expiry of 8 hours, with the structure {expiry_unix}:{account_index}:{api_key_index}:{random_hex}. REST sends the token as the Authorization header; WebSocket sends it as "auth" inside the subscribe message. Authenticating a request makes it count against the L1 address instead of the IP. Read-only tokens (structure ro:{account_index}:{single|all}:{expiry_unix}:{random_hex}) cannot sign transactions, have a maximum expiry of 10 years and a minimum of 5 minutes, and cover one account index (single) or the master account and its sub-accounts (all). On Lighter, tokens/create costs 10,000 request weight, so create tokens once and store them. Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Hard-coded numbers in third-party connectors can disagree with Lighter's docs. Hummingbot's Lighter connector constants say the table matches the docs exactly, yet encode Plus sendTx at 8,000 per minute, a Plus read pool of 120,000 weighted requests and Premium sendTx of 4,000–40,000 depending on staked LIT. Lighter's mainnet docs list Plus at 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium up to 72000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute. Read the live docs instead of copying numbers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/blob/3351adad0a09f6a57a202219d3e52fe794672421/hummingbot/connector/exchange/lighter/lighter_constants.py · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] In October 2025 a bot error pushed HYPE to $98 on Lighter, at a steep premium compared to global prices. Lighter said a runaway bot jammed through the HYPE book with size, that low volume was traded at very high prices, that there were no liquidations or other adverse effects, and that the wick was scrubbed from the front end. Crypto analyst Duo Nine, quoted by CoinDesk, said removing the data masks deeper liquidity issues. Lighter's docs make price on a taker order the worst acceptable price: if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price, the order is cancelled. (high confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/1982936377668022508 · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/10/28/how-a-bot-glitch-sent-hyperliquid-s-hype-token-soaring-to-usd98, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Premium/Advanced sendTx/sendTxBatch capacity scales with staked LIT: 4000 per minute at 0 LIT, 5000 at 1000, 12000 at 100000, 24000 at 300000 and 72000 at 500000. Lighter documents 72,000 transactions per minute as the Premium/Advanced maximum on Lighter mainnet (24,000 on Robinhood Chain). Fee credits count as staked LIT for this purpose. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota
- [statement] Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts are gated by a volume quota that is enforced only for those tiers. Only L2CreateOrder, L2CancelAllOrders, L2ModifyOrder and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume quota; single-order cancels do not. Quota is earned per fill at 1 quota per $1 or $2 of notional depending on the market, shared across sub-accounts of one L1 address, and every 15 seconds the account gets one free sendTx. A sendTxBatch of n transactions consumes n quota. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits
- [statement] Per-account order caps differ by tier. Standard allows 50 pending (TP/SL/TWAP) and 250 active orders per account, with 10 pending and 30 active per market. Premium/Advanced allows 1000 pending and 1500 active per account, with 100 pending and 1000 active per market. Transaction-type limits apply to all tiers, for example 40 requests/minute by default and for L2UpdateLeverage, and 2 requests/minute plus 3 per 2 hours for L2Withdraw. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits
- [statement] API trading goes through the sendTx and sendTxBatch REST endpoints or the jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch WebSocket types. Every transaction is signed with SignerClient, which uses a signer binary whose code is in the public lighter-go repo. Each order carries a nonce, integer prices and sizes, and a client order index unique across all markets. HTTP code=200 only means the syntax was accepted; the sequencer can still reject the order. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/blob/main/lighter/signer_client.py, https://github.com/smohantty/lighter-trading-bot
- [statement] On 16 Nov 2026 one transfer of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC (about 10.39 million USDC) left Lighter's Ethereum contract to a single wallet, which Bitquery traced through CoW Swap to ETH and on toward Hyperliquid. Lighter said its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure and official SDKs were not compromised. Lighter paused withdrawals and pool creation and switched on Guardian mode; Guardian mode was later disabled, withdrawals resumed, and its Security Council returned approximately $5 million in USDC to the affected trader. (high confidence) — https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://mlq.ai/news/crypto-exchange-lighter-pauses-withdrawals-after-about-10-million-is-drained-through-a-leaked-api-key/, https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/
- [statement] Per Lighter's postmortem as reported by Crypto Briefing, the affected accounts used signing code outside the official SDKs that repeatedly reused cryptographic nonces, so private keys could be reconstructed from publicly available signatures. The attacker used the keys to create a public pool from the affected account, acquired pool shares through a separate account, transferred the victim's funds into the pool and redeemed the shares. (medium confidence) — https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/ · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.blockhead.co/2026/11/18/api-keys-are-the-new-hot-wallet-lighter-luxor-and-signalplus-show-how-credentials-beat-contracts/
- [statement] After the incident Lighter requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools and made API key signatures nonpublic. It plans to introduce IP allowlists, configurable API key permissions and automated monitoring for nonce reuse, and advised traders using custom or third party signing software to rotate their API keys and switch to its official SDKs. Lighter's documentation says API keys can place trades, manage positions and move funds between accounts tied to the same wallet, as reported by Cointelegraph via MLQ. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17) — https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/ · keywords: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.tradingview.com/news/cointelegraph:6f3e2fa08094b:0-lighter-incident-exposes-risks-beyond-withdrawal-controls/, https://mlq.ai/news/crypto-exchange-lighter-pauses-withdrawals-after-about-10-million-is-drained-through-a-leaked-api-key/
